newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - GA rejects acquistions near term.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - GA rejects acquistions near term.

text.p: General Accident said on Tuesday it did not envisage any major acquistions in its drive to build the company's presence in the UK life market in the short term.
"At the present time there's nothing wrong with organic growth in life. We've proved we're capable of achieving that," General Accident chief executive Bob Scott told Reuters in an interview.
Scott was speaking as the group reported operating profits for the year of 421 million pounds, a fall over the year but ahead of analyst forecasts.
A change in the way currency movements are accounted for added 10 million pounds to the profits.
"The key for the life company is the profitability of new business. We've done very well in a year where we've had a pretty big reorganisation. We're confident we can build on it," said Scott.
Provident Mutual, acquired in January 1996, contributed 18 million pounds to the results, net of reorganisation costs of 16 million pounds.
"Provident Mutual brought pension expertise which we had been after for some time. We have to capitalise on that now," added Scott.
